summary: This Makefile snippet defines a task called 'runsql' that checks whether a SQL variable has been set, then either prints a yellow message saying what SQL will run, or prints a red error message and exits if SQL wasn't provided. It's a safety check to prevent accidentally running undefined SQL commands.

explanations.1: This creates a variable named COLOR_RED with the value 31, which is an ANSI color code that terminals use to display text in red.
explanations.2: This creates a variable named COLOR_YELLOW with the value 33, which is an ANSI color code for yellow text.
explanations.5: The ${SQL} checks if the SQL variable is set; if it is, the first part runs (showing yellow text), otherwise the second part runs after the || (showing red text and exiting with error code 1). The \e[1;...m sequences are escape codes that tell the terminal to start coloring, and \e[0m turns coloring off.
